novum_candidates.description: The story is set in a freshly created, still-being-finished world (Eden/Garden) in which cosmological and natural features are literal artifacts of a recent act of creation: mountains left ragged, plains cluttered, the moon coming loose and falling out of the sky, and stars that can be reached at the rim of the circle. This totalizing 'newly-minted cosmos' frames the narrator's entire existence and epistemology.

novelty.rationale: The world is presented as a recently constructed artifact, materially different from the empirical norm: mountains are 'left in a ragged condition' after a rush of finishing, and the moon literally 'got loose' and 'fell out of the scheme.' This is a totalizing difference altering the story universe's cosmology.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The created-world premise draws on a religious/mythic creation frame (the Garden, the Fall) rather than an immanent nonsupernatural account. The 'scheme,' the makers who return the moon, and the Giver point to a supernatural rather than systematic imaginary-science logic, leaving cognitive validation uncertain.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The freshly-created world governs the whole narrative: the diary form, the naming of creatures, the naive cosmology, and ultimately the loss of the Garden after the Fall all flow from this premise.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The narrator's literal beliefs (moon falling out, stars melting, water running uphill in the dark) contrast sharply with reader knowledge of empirical physics, producing estrangement through a defamiliarized cosmos.

novum_candidates.description: The narrator is a being who came into existence 'a day ago' and constructs knowledge of the entire world from scratch through observation, experiment, naming, and axiom-formation. She invents empirical method (proving by experiment), names all creatures instantly, and identifies fire as a wholly new thing she has created.

novelty.rationale: A one-day-old adult consciousness building all knowledge from zero, naming every creature as 'the first,' and literally 'adding a new thing to the world' (fire) departs totally from the empirical norm of gradual human development.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The narrator develops a coherent, systematic (if error-prone) empirical methodology: forming axioms, insisting on demonstration, and reasoning from cumulative evidence. This is an immanent, nonsupernatural cognitive process even where conclusions are faulty.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The entire text is the first-person record of this newborn cognizing narrator; her process of discovery, naming, and experiment structures every episode and constitutes the narrative's overriding logic.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The reader recognizes fire, men, stars, and hydrology that the newborn narrator misidentifies (a man as a reptile, stars that melt, water running uphill in the dark), estranging familiar things through the eyes of a first cognizer.

novum_candidates.description: The narrator accidentally produces fire by boring a stick, recognizes it as a wholly new thing, and reflects that she has 'added a new thing to the world's uncountable properties.'

novelty.rationale: Fire is presented as literally the first fire, smoke, and flames ever to exist in the world, a new property added to the universe.

cognitive_validation.rationale: Fire arises through an immanent, nonsupernatural mechanical process (boring a dry stick), a coherent causal account.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: Fire is a single memorable episode and a device revealing character contrast; it does not determine the overriding narrative logic, which is driven by the narrator's cognition and the relationship with Adam. It is incidental relative to the whole diary.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The reader knows fire as commonplace, but the narrator's wonder at its first-ever appearance and her discovery of fear through it defamiliarizes it.
